title: A ring buffer for the gate log

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own project brief, code, tests and rubric for a ring buffer for the gate log, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

brief: The hostel gate's entry terminal has very little memory, so it keeps only the newest N log lines and quietly drops the oldest. Build that log as a ring buffer in C: a fixed block of memory, two counters and modular arithmetic, with no shifting of entries and no unbounded copies.
requirements: INIT allocates room for N entries once (1 ≤ N ≤ 1000).
PUSH stores the text (cut to 47 characters); when full it overwrites the oldest entry.
LAST k prints up to k entries, newest first.
COUNT reports how many entries are kept and how many were ever pushed; CLEAR empties the log but keeps the pushed total.
io_protocol:
| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `INIT <n>` | `log of <n> entries` |
| `PUSH <text>` | `ok <total pushed>` |
| `LAST <k>` | `<i>: <entry>` for the newest k entries, newest first, or `empty` |
| `COUNT` | `<kept> kept, <pushed> pushed` |
| `CLEAR` | `cleared` |

Before INIT every command prints `error: no log yet`; anything else prints `error: bad command <line>`.

milestones.title: Push and read back
milestones.instructions: Implement `ring_push` and `ring_newest`. Never move entries: only `start` and `count` change.
hints: The next free slot is (start + count) % capacity.
When full, the slot to write is start, and start moves forward by one.
The k-th newest is at (start + count - 1 - k) % capacity.

milestones.title: Clear
milestones.instructions: Implement `ring_clear` without freeing memory; the pushed total stays.
hints: Resetting start and count is enough: old text is simply never read again.

rubric.criterion: Hidden tests pass: every command prints exactly the expected output.
Entries are never shifted; all writes are bounded by ENTRY_LEN; malloc is checked and freed once.
Readable names, small functions and clear error handling (AI feedback, advice only).

extensions: Add LAST-MATCH <word> that prints the newest entry containing the word.
Store a timestamp with each entry.
